events.title: CBN rate decision — 307th MPC meeting
events.summary: The CBN sets the benchmark interest rate. This decision flows into every savings rate, bond rate and T-bill yield in the country within weeks.

events.title: CBN rate decision — 308th MPC meeting
events.summary: The last rate decision of 2026. Whatever is set here governs what your money earns going into the new year.

events.title: FGN Savings Bond — September offer
events.summary: The federal government borrows directly from ordinary Nigerians. You lend them money for 2 or 3 years and they pay you interest every quarter.
howTo: Contact a stockbroking firm appointed as a DMO distribution agent
You will need your BVN and a bank account in your own name
Subscribe in multiples of ₦1,000 above the ₦5,000 minimum
Interest lands quarterly — 16 Dec, 16 Mar, 16 Jun, 16 Sep

events.title: FGN Savings Bond — October offer
events.summary: The next monthly window. The DMO publishes the circular in the first week of the month, and the rate is only known then.
howTo: Watch for the October circular on dmo.gov.ng in the first week
Line up your broker or bank investment desk before it opens
The window runs Monday to Friday — five working days, no extensions
events.expectedNote: Dates follow the DMO monthly pattern. The October circular had not been published when this was checked — confirm before acting.

events.title: NBS inflation figures — September data
events.summary: The official measure of how fast prices are rising. This is the number your investments have to beat just to keep your money from shrinking.
events.expectedNote: The NBS releases each month CPI on the 15th of the following month, or the next working day.

events.title: NBS inflation figures — October data
events.summary: The next inflation print. Landing just before the November MPC meeting, it is the figure the committee will be reacting to.
events.expectedNote: The 15th falls on a Sunday, so the release moves to Monday 16 November.

events.title: Dangote Refinery share offer (IPO)
events.summary: The refinery is selling shares to the public for the first time — the first refinery ever offered on the Nigerian Exchange. Buying shares makes you part-owner of the business, so what you get back depends on how it performs. Unlike a bond, nothing is guaranteed.
events.tenor: No end date — you hold the shares until you sell them
howTo: You need a CSCS account, which your broker or investment app opens for you
Subscribe through NGX Invest, a licensed stockbroker, or an SEC-registered investment app
Check any platform on the SEC register at sec.gov.ng before you send money
Decide your amount before you start: shares can fall as well as rise, and this is not a fixed return
Applications close on 13 October — allotment and listing follow afterwards

events.title: FGN Savings Bond — November offer
events.summary: The government borrows from ordinary savers for two or three years and pays you a fixed rate every quarter. September paid 15.12% on the 3-year: on ₦100,000 that is ₦3,780 landing in your account every three months, then your ₦100,000 back at the end.
howTo: Watch dmo.gov.ng for the November circular in the first week
Contact a DMO-appointed stockbroker or your bank’s investment desk before it opens
You need a bank account in your own name, your BVN and a valid ID
The window runs Monday to Friday — five working days, no extensions
events.expectedNote: The DMO opens this window in the first full week of each month. The circular for this month had not been published when this was checked — confirm the dates and the rate before acting.

events.title: FGN Bond auction — October
events.summary: The government’s main monthly borrowing, in bonds lasting ten years or more. The minimum at the auction itself is ₦50 million, so this is not where most people buy — but the rate set here is the anchor every other rate follows, and you can buy the same bonds in small amounts afterwards through a broker.
events.rate: Set at auction — September’s new 10-year cleared at 16.79%
events.minimum: ₦50,000,000 at the auction · from about ₦10,000 through a broker afterwards
howTo: Most people do not bid here. Watch the rate instead: it tells you where all other rates are heading
To own these bonds in a smaller amount, ask a stockbroker about buying on the secondary market
The DMO publishes the offer circular about a week before the auction
events.expectedNote: The DMO holds one FGN Bond auction a month; September’s was on Monday the 14th, settling on the 16th. The Q4 2026 issuance calendar had not been published when this was checked.

events.title: Treasury Bill auction — 7 October
events.summary: Short-term government borrowing, in 91, 182 and 364-day bills. You are not paid interest: you buy the bill for less than it repays. A 364-day bill clearing at 15.89%, September’s rate, means paying about ₦86,300 today for ₦100,000 in a year — the ₦13,700 gap is your return, and it is tax-free.
events.rate: Set at auction — the 364-day bill cleared at 15.89% on 23 September
events.minimum: ₦50,000,000 at the auction · from about ₦100,000 through a bank or broker
howTo: The auction itself is for large institutions. To buy a smaller parcel, ask your bank’s treasury desk or a stockbroker
Ask what rate they are offering and compare it with the auction rate — the gap is their margin
Your money is returned in full at maturity, and the return is not taxed
events.expectedNote: The CBN auctions Treasury Bills on Wednesdays, roughly twice a month. The last auction of Q3 was 23 September and the Q4 programme had not been published when this was checked, so this date is an estimate from the usual pattern. Confirm on cbn.gov.ng.

events.title: NBS inflation figures — November data
events.summary: The official measure of how fast prices are rising. This is the number every investment has to beat just to keep your money where it is. August came in at 15.39%, the third monthly fall in a row.
howTo: The report is published on nigerianstat.gov.ng, usually mid-morning
Compare the headline figure with the rate you are earning — the gap is what you are really making
events.expectedNote: NBS publishes the CPI report in the middle of the following month. The exact date for this release had not been announced when this was checked.
